title: Translation units, declarations, definitions and external linkage
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: A translation unit is the source file after preprocessing. Declarations introduce identifiers and types; definitions provide entities or storage. External linkage allows compatible declarations in different translation units to refer to the same function or object.
understand.whyItMatters: Multi-file programs depend on consistent declarations and exactly appropriate definitions. Linkage errors can arise from missing or duplicate definitions and inconsistent interfaces.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.
